rules.title: Google Chrome cache
rules.explanation: Copies of pages, images and scripts Chrome keeps so sites load faster.
rules.ifRemoved: Chrome downloads them again as you browse. Sites may load a little slower at first.

rules.title: Chrome update copies
rules.explanation: Copies of Chrome that macOS keeps while Chrome updates itself. They're clones of the app, so they share its space on disk.
rules.ifRemoved: Chrome makes new copies when it needs them. Removing them frees little or no space.

rules.title: Visual Studio Code cache
rules.explanation: Compiled code, data and extension downloads VS Code keeps so it starts faster.
rules.ifRemoved: VS Code rebuilds them. The next launch may be a little slower.

rules.title: Xcode build data
rules.explanation: Intermediate build products and indexes Xcode creates for each project.
rules.ifRemoved: Xcode recreates them. The next build of each project takes longer.

rules.title: Go build cache
rules.explanation: Compiled packages the Go toolchain keeps to speed up builds.
rules.ifRemoved: Go rebuilds what it needs. The next build of each project is slower.

rules.title: Homebrew downloads
rules.explanation: Package files Homebrew downloaded to install or upgrade software.
rules.ifRemoved: Installed software keeps working. Homebrew downloads a file again only if you reinstall that package.

rules.title: Swift Package Manager cache
rules.explanation: Swift packages downloaded for your projects.
rules.ifRemoved: Swift downloads packages again the next time a project needs them.

rules.title: npm cache
rules.explanation: Packages npm downloaded, kept so installs are faster.
rules.ifRemoved: npm downloads packages again when a project needs them.

rules.title: Yarn cache
rules.explanation: Packages Yarn downloaded, kept so installs are faster.
rules.ifRemoved: Yarn downloads packages again when a project needs them.

rules.title: pip cache
rules.explanation: Python packages pip downloaded or built.
rules.ifRemoved: pip downloads packages again when you install them.

rules.title: CocoaPods cache
rules.explanation: Pods CocoaPods downloaded for your projects.
rules.ifRemoved: CocoaPods downloads them again on the next pod install.

rules.title: Playwright test browsers
rules.explanation: Browsers Playwright downloaded to run automated tests.
rules.ifRemoved: Playwright downloads them again on the next test run, which can take several minutes.

rules.title: Hugging Face models
rules.explanation: AI models and datasets downloaded by tools that use Hugging Face.
rules.ifRemoved: They download again when a tool needs them, which can take a long time for large models.

rules.title: Ollama models
rules.explanation: AI models downloaded with Ollama.
rules.ifRemoved: Ollama downloads a model again the next time you run it.

rules.title: Command-line tool caches
rules.explanation: Caches that command-line tools keep in the hidden .cache folder.
rules.ifRemoved: Each tool rebuilds its cache when it needs it.

rules.title: Old crash reports
rules.explanation: Reports macOS wrote when apps crashed or stopped responding.
rules.ifRemoved: Nothing changes. Reports from the last 30 days are kept for troubleshooting.

rules.title: npm logs
rules.explanation: Logs npm writes for each command.
rules.ifRemoved: Nothing changes; npm writes new logs as needed.

rules.title: App logs
rules.explanation: Activity logs apps write for troubleshooting.
rules.ifRemoved: Apps start new logs. Only logs untouched for a week are listed.

rules.title: Temporary files
rules.explanation: Files apps made for short-term use and didn't clean up.
rules.ifRemoved: Nothing that's still in use is listed: only items untouched for 3 days.

rules.title: macOS caches
rules.explanation: Caches used by macOS and Apple apps.
rules.ifRemoved: macOS rebuilds them, but some are in use right now. They're usually small.

rules.title: App caches
rules.explanation: Data apps keep to work faster, such as downloaded images, previews and web content.
rules.ifRemoved: Apps rebuild their caches as you use them.

locations.title: SSH keys
locations.explanation: Keys that sign you in to servers and services such as GitHub.

locations.title: Encryption keys
locations.explanation: GnuPG keys for signing and encrypting.

locations.title: Command-line tool settings
locations.explanation: Settings for command-line tools you use.

locations.title: Command-line tools and their data
locations.explanation: Programs installed just for your account, and the data they keep.

locations.title: npm data
locations.explanation: npm's download cache and logs. Raker lists the parts that are safe to remove.

locations.title: Command-line tool caches
locations.explanation: Caches kept by command-line tools. Raker lists them one tool at a time.

locations.title: Visual Studio Code extensions
locations.explanation: Extensions you installed in VS Code. Remove them from inside VS Code.

locations.title: Docker settings
locations.explanation: Docker's configuration and sign-in data. Images and containers are stored elsewhere.

locations.title: Terminal session history
locations.explanation: Command history Terminal saves for each window.

locations.title: Trash
locations.explanation: Items you moved to the Trash.

locations.title: Gradle data
locations.explanation: Gradle's caches and downloaded dependencies.

locations.title: Maven repository
locations.explanation: Java libraries Maven downloaded.

locations.title: Rust packages and tools
locations.explanation: Rust's package registry cache and tools you installed with cargo.

locations.title: Rust toolchains
locations.explanation: Rust compilers installed with rustup.

locations.title: Ollama
locations.explanation: Ollama's AI models and settings.

locations.title: App caches
locations.explanation: Data apps keep to work faster. Apps rebuild their caches as needed.

locations.title: App data
locations.explanation: Documents, settings and databases apps keep for you. This isn't a cache: an app's folder should only go when you uninstall the app.

locations.title: App logs
locations.explanation: Logs and crash reports from apps.

locations.title: macOS per-user working area
locations.explanation: macOS keeps temporary files (T), caches (C) and app copies (X) here, and cleans much of it automatically.

locations.title: Shared temporary folder
locations.explanation: Temporary files from apps and tools. macOS empties it when the Mac restarts.
